sentinel: SUCCESS:RES-0070 in the receipt AND a field-by-field cache-key specification plus a named uncacheable step class

cache_key_specification.description: field-by-field cache-key specification: every listed field must enter the key of a cacheable agent step; omitting any one field collides two steps that differ only in that field.

fields.bazel_nix_analog: Bazel fingerprints the action mnemonic in SpawnAction.computeKey (fp.addString(mnemonic)).
fields.justification: Two different step kinds (retrieve vs. synthesize vs. tool-call) must not share a memo slot. The mnemonic is the cheapest collision-breaker and is already in Bazel's action key.
fields.omit_failure: retrieve and synthesize collide on the same prompt.

fields.bazel_nix_analog: Tool/compiler identity: a hermetic build pins the toolchain. Nix input-address is a function of the derivation, including the builder.
fields.justification: The catalog names model version as a first-class input. The same prompt through provider:model:revision A and B is a different action. Identity is provider + model id + snapshot/revision, not a marketing name.

fields.bazel_nix_analog: Command-line analog. SpawnAction.computeKey adds commandLines to the fingerprint. Temperature is a declared execution parameter.
fields.justification: Temperature, top_p, max_tokens, and seed (when present) change the output distribution. Omitting temperature makes T=0 and T=1 share a key, which is the exact unsound-cache-key defect.

fields.bazel_nix_analog: Declared input file contents. Bazel hashes input files, not paths. DVC: file hashes are calculated from file contents only.
fields.justification: The prompt/system/tool-preamble is the primary declared input. Hash the exact bytes sent, not a template id that can be edited underfoot.

fields.bazel_nix_analog: Command line / toolchain files: available tools change the action.
fields.justification: Which tools the model may call, and their JSON schemas, change behavior. A policy digest belongs in the key the same way argv does.
fields.omit_failure: read-only vs. write-enabled tool sets collide.

fields.bazel_nix_analog: Bazel: required inputs are declared explicitly for each action. Nix: input-addressed output path is a function of the derivation inputs.
fields.justification: Attached files, prior-step outputs, and retrieved blobs enter as content hashes (sorted), never as workspace paths.

fields.bazel_nix_analog: Source identity is a content hash (Git / file digest), not a URL. Bazel hermeticity: isolate the build from host-system change.
fields.justification: A live web source is an input. The URL is a path. The captured response body (plus final URL after redirects and HTTP status) must be snapshotted and hashed into the key. If no snapshot exists, the step is not cacheable — see uncacheable class live-web-unsapped-search-then-reason.
fields.omit_failure: same URL, different page body, same key (stale serve).

fields.bazel_nix_analog: Only environment variables explicitly whitelisted via --action_env are included in a Bazel action definition. Undeclared $PATH differences otherwise prevent (or silently poison) cache hits.
fields.justification: Declared env (region, feature flags) that the step is allowed to read. Secrets never enter the key; they also must not enter the action.

claims.canonical_mechanism: Bazel memoizes an action by hashing the declared action: mnemonic, command line, declared environment, and declared inputs. The remote cache is a map of those action hashes to result metadata plus a content-addressable store of output files. Undeclared host state is not in the key.

quotes: The action cache, which is a map of action hashes to action result metadata.
A content-addressable store (CAS) of output files.
has inputs, output names, a command line, and environment variables.
inputs and expected outputs are declared explicitly for each action.

claims.strongest_caveat: SpawnAction.computeKey is the spawn-shaped action; other action subclasses add their own fields. The mapping to agent steps is analogical, not a claim that Bazel will cache an LLM.

claims.canonical_mechanism: Nix input-addressing names a store object by how it was made: the output path is a function of the derivation (hashQuotientDerivation / derivation modulo), not of the output bytes. The store-path fingerprint is type:sha256:inner-digest:store:name.

quotes: the input-addressed derivation has an input address
function not of the output itself, but of the derivation that produced it.

claims.strongest_caveat: Fixed-output (content-addressed) derivations are a different addressing mode. This unit uses the input-addressed case as the analog for 'hash the recipe'.

claims.canonical_mechanism: An agent-step cache key that is honest about Bazel/Nix must include, field by field: step mnemonic, model identity (provider + id + revision), sampling parameters (including temperature), prompt-bytes sha256, tool-policy sha256, declared input-artifact sha256s, live-source snapshot sha256 (captured body, not URL), and declared env. Omitting any field makes two distinct steps collide.

quotes: hash inputs to look up in the cache.

claims.strongest_caveat: This is a specification plus a collision test, not a measurement of any production agent cache. Live-web without a snapshot is not a key field — it is uncacheable (C4).

claims.canonical_mechanism: Named uncacheable step class live-web-unsapped-search-then-reason: a step whose output depends on a live web fetch or search index result that was not captured as declared input bytes before the model call. There is no content digest to put in the key. URL-only keying collides two different bodies. The honest mark is uncacheable, not a partial key.

quotes: hash inputs to look up in the cache.

claims.strongest_caveat: A captured, hashed snapshot of the page (plus HTTP status and final URL) makes the step cacheable under C3. Non-seeded positive temperature is a second uncacheable class for exact-output memoization.

legacy_root.question: Bazel and Nix cache on a hash of inputs — for an agent step whose output depends on a model version, a temperature, and a live web source, what exactly must enter the cache key, and which steps are honestly not cacheable at all?

supporting_e3.reason: Live dvc.org returned HTTP 429. One Wayback prose rail remains; a claim with one rail is E3 and is not cited as measured fact.

legacy_root.title: Assess content-addressed memoization for agent steps: what is safely cacheable

uncacheable_step_classes.control: Two fetches of one URL with different bodies must not share a cache slot. A URL-only mutant key collides; the classifier refuses to emit a key at all.
uncacheable_step_classes.definition: A step whose output depends on a live web fetch or search-index result that was not captured as declared input bytes (body sha256, final URL, HTTP status, fetch timestamp) before the model call.
uncacheable_step_classes.title: Live-web unsapped search-then-reason
uncacheable_step_classes.why_not_cacheable: There is no content digest to put in the key. Keying by URL is unsound: the same URL can yield different bodies. Bazel analog: an undeclared host input / non-hermetic action. Nix analog: an impurity. The honest mark is uncacheable, not a partial key.

uncacheable_step_classes.control: classify() returns this class; compute_key() raises UncacheableStep.
uncacheable_step_classes.definition: Exact-output memoization of a step with temperature > 0, no seed, and no documented deterministic decoding.
uncacheable_step_classes.title: Non-deterministic sampler (exact-output memoization)
uncacheable_step_classes.why_not_cacheable: The output is not a function of the declared inputs. A cache hit would pretend replay. Distributional caches are a different contract and are out of scope for this unit.
